question: The formation of World Trade Organisation (WTO) was preceded by: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: General Agreement on Trade in Services
General Agreement on Intellectual Property Rights
Multilateral Trade Agreement
General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs

Explanation:
The World Trade Organisation (WTO) came into existence on 1 January 1995. It replaced the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), which was established in 1947 to reduce trade barriers and tariffs among member countries. GATT provided a framework for negotiating tariff reductions and resolving trade disputes. The WTO expanded the scope of trade rules to include services (GATS), intellectual property (TRIPS), and a stronger dispute settlement mechanism. Thus, before the formation of WTO, the General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs (GATT) was the governing body for international trade.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When did WTO come into existence? → 1 January 1995
☛ When was GATT established? → 1947
☛ Where is WTO headquarters located? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ Under which agreement was WTO formed? → Marrakesh Agreement (1994)
☛ How many member countries are in WTO as of 2025? → 164

options_hi: सेवाओं में व्यापार पर सामान्य समझौता
बौद्धिक संपदा अधिकारों पर सामान्य समझौता
बहुपक्षीय व्यापार समझौता
व्यापार और टैरिफ पर सामान्य समझौता
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है व्यापार और टैरिफ पर सामान्य समझौता

Explanation:
विश्व व्यापार संगठन (WTO) का गठन 1 जनवरी 1995 को हुआ था। इससे पहले अंतर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार को नियंत्रित करने वाला मुख्य समझौता GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) था, जिसे 1947 में लागू किया गया था। GATT का उद्देश्य सदस्य देशों के बीच व्यापार बाधाओं को कम करना और टैरिफ में कटौती करना था। WTO ने GATT की जगह ली और व्यापार के नियमों को सेवाओं (GATS), बौद्धिक संपदा (TRIPS) और विवाद निपटान तंत्र तक विस्तारित किया। इस प्रकार WTO के गठन से पहले General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs (व्यापार और टैरिफ पर सामान्य समझौता) लागू था।

question: Who was the first European president of the Indian National Congress? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (16/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Annie Besant
George Yule
AO Hume
Alfred Webb
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is George Yule

Explanation:
The first European president of the Indian National Congress was George Yule. He presided over the 1888 session in Allahabad. George Yule was a British-born businessman associated with a prominent trading house in Calcutta. In the early years of Congress, there were several British members, but Yule was the first European to be elected as president. Subsequently, Alfred Webb (1894) and Annie Besant (1917) also became presidents. A.O. Hume was the founder of Congress but never served as its president.

question: Gurdwara Panja Sahib is located in ____________. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (01/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Canada
India

Sri Lanka
solution:

Explanation:
Gurdwara Panja Sahib is located in Hasan Abdal, Punjab province, Pakistan. It is one of the most sacred Sikh pilgrimage sites. The name 'Panja Sahib' refers to the handprint of Guru Nanak Dev on a rock. According to tradition, Guru Nanak stopped a rolling boulder with his hand, leaving his palm imprint. This gurdwara holds immense religious significance for Sikhs, who visit it from around the world. The site is associated with a miracle and is a symbol of faith. Hassan Abdal is a city in the Rawalpindi District of Punjab, Pakistan.

question: A new dimension added by Amartya Sen to food security is: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: entitlements
availability of food
affordability
sustainable livelihoods
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is entitlements

Explanation:
Amartya Sen introduced a new dimension to the concept of food security, known as entitlements. He argued that food security is not just about the availability of food or its affordability, but also about an individual's ability to command that food. In his influential work 'Poverty and Famines', Sen demonstrated that famines occur not because of food shortage but due to the failure of entitlement—people lose the legal, social, or economic means to obtain food. Therefore, food security must include the aspect of entitlement, which refers to the set of commodity bundles that a person can legitimately acquire using their resources and rights. This dimension shifts the focus from food supply to people's capacity to access food.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ New dimension added by Amartya Sen to food security → Entitlements
☛ Main cause of famines according to Sen → Lack of access to food, not food shortage
☛ Famous book by Amartya Sen → Poverty and Famines
☛ Meaning of entitlement → Legal or social right to obtain a commodity
☛ Traditional dimensions of food security → Availability, affordability, sustainable livelihoods

question: Qila Mubarak monument is situated in_____. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: Punjab
Haryana
Rajasthan

question: Which among the following organisations is the best example of an agreement between oligopolists? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/04/2021) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following Indian musicologists is recognised for his role in organising and codifying Hindustani classical music, thereby laying the groundwork for modern education of India's musical heritage? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 1)

Ustad Abdul Karim Khan
Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande

Explanation:
Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande (1860-1936) is recognized for organizing and codifying Hindustani classical music, laying the groundwork for modern music education. He traveled across India, collecting ragas from different gharanas and systematizing them. In his seminal work 'Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati', he classified ragas into ten thaats (parent scales) based on scientific principles. This provided a standardized curriculum for music colleges and established a structured pedagogy. Bhatkhande founded the Music College in Baroda (Vadodara) and promoted the academic study of Indian music. His efforts transformed Hindustani music into a disciplined, teachable art form, which continues to be the foundation of music education today.

question: Which of the following eminent persons called the Indian Constitution as 'Lawyer’s Paradise and difficult to understand by common Citizen'? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 2)

question: Which institution was established in 1921 as a deliberative body for princes? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Chamber of Princes
Indian Council
Imperial Assembly
Royal Consultation Board
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chamber of Princes

Explanation:
The Chamber of Princes (Narendra Mandal) was established in 1921 as a deliberative and advisory body for the rulers of Indian princely states. It was inaugurated on February 8, 1921, by Viceroy Lord Reading. Its purpose was to provide a platform for princes to discuss matters of common interest and convey their views to the British government. The Chamber consisted of representatives from over 108 princely states, but major states like Hyderabad and Mysore did not join. It remained functional until 1947 and was dissolved after India's independence.

question: Which of the following is a musical instrument that consists of a set of glass, metal or clay bowls, each having varying levels of water? (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 2)
